stories.headline: Mathematician accuses OpenAI of muscling in on his AI-assisted fluid dynamics breakthrough

key_facts.fact: NYU Courant mathematician Tristan Buckmaster and Anthropic researcher Levent Alpoge published on 8 September 2026 three Lean-verified results proving finite-time blow-up with smooth forcing for incompressible porous media, Boussinesq and 3D incompressible Euler equations.
key_facts.excerpt: Today, Levent Alpoge and I have made public three results: finite-time blowup with smooth forcing for incompressible porous media, for Boussinesq, and for 3d incompressible Euler.

key_facts.fact: Buckmaster says the pair used Anthropic's Claude and OpenAI's Codex (with GPT-5.6 Sol and Astra) to push a research program originated by Diego Cordoba and Luis Martinez-Zoroa from rough forcing to smooth forcing.
key_facts.excerpt: We used several LLMs throughout: Anthropic's Claude, OpenAI's Codex, especially with GPT-5.6 Sol and, more recently, Astra.

key_facts.fact: Buckmaster says he was told on 6 September by OpenAI's Sebastien Bubeck that an internal OpenAI model had produced a roughly 100-page proof of finite-time blow-up for forced Navier-Stokes, and that OpenAI eventually conceded its first prompt on the problem was sent only after word of Buckmaster's work reached the company.
key_facts.excerpt: Eventually it was agreed that it had been sent in the past few days, after information about our work had reached OpenAI.

key_facts.fact: Buckmaster says he asked whether the OpenAI model had been trained on or had access to his Codex sessions, where he had stored all project drafts; he was told the model did not look up user data but got no answer on training.
key_facts.excerpt: I was told the model did not look up user data. I asked again, about training, and I did not get an answer.

key_facts.fact: Buckmaster alleges Bubeck twice pushed to remove Alpoge from authorship because Alpoge works at Anthropic, and that when Buckmaster said he would go public, Bubeck replied 'Why would you ruin your career?'
key_facts.excerpt: Sebastien twice asserted that he wanted Levent removed from authorship... The reply was, 'Why would you ruin your career?'

key_facts.fact: Bubeck publicly called the allegations 'false and inflammatory' on X, said he entered the discussion 'following academic norms', and promised a fuller response.
key_facts.excerpt: Bubeck's statement, posted to X, reads in part that he came into the discussion 'following academic norms'

key_facts.fact: OpenAI says an internal model 'significantly more capable than GPT-6 Astra' solved the Navier-Stokes problem using 10,000 concurrent agents working for 88 hours, and denies its researchers or models saw Buckmaster or Alpoge's prompts.
key_facts.excerpt: OpenAI says an internal model 'significantly more capable than GPT-6 Astra' solved the Navier-Stokes problem using 10K concurrent agents working for 88 hours

key_facts.fact: Fields medalist Terence Tao called the Buckmaster-Alpoge work a remarkable achievement; the results stop short of the unforced Navier-Stokes Millennium Prize problem, which carries a $1 million Clay Institute award.
key_facts.excerpt: This is significant but still stops short of the Clay Millennium Prize. That prize asks about the unforced Navier-Stokes equations.

stories.headline: Mistral raises EUR 3B led by Samsung at EUR 21B, Europe's largest-ever equity round

key_facts.fact: Mistral announced on 8 September 2026 a EUR 3 billion Series D at a post-money valuation of more than EUR 21 billion, which it calls the largest equity fundraising ever completed by a European technology company.
key_facts.excerpt: Mistral today announced that it has raised EUR 3 billion in a Series D funding round at a post-money valuation of more than EUR 21 billion, the largest equity fundraising round ever completed by a European technology company, three years after the company's launch.

key_facts.fact: Samsung Electronics led the round, co-led by the EQT-managed Scaleup Europe Fund and existing investor PSG Equity; Mistral's previous Series C was led by chip-equipment maker ASML.
key_facts.excerpt: Samsung Electronics led the round, joined by co-leads Scaleup Europe Fund, managed by EQT, and existing investor PSG Equity.

key_facts.fact: The valuation nearly doubles the EUR 11.7 billion Mistral was worth after its EUR 1.7 billion Series C a year earlier.
key_facts.excerpt: Mistral was valued at EUR 11.7 billion in 2025 after a EUR 1.7 billion Series C led by Dutch chipmaker ASML, meaning the company has almost doubled its valuation in a year.

key_facts.fact: New investors include Advent, funds managed by BlackRock and the Grand Duchy of Luxembourg; returning backers include a16z, ASML, Nvidia, Salesforce Ventures, General Catalyst, Index Ventures and Bpifrance.
key_facts.excerpt: New investors in the round include Advent, funds and accounts managed by BlackRock, and the Grand Duchy of Luxembourg.

key_facts.fact: Mistral has now disclosed roughly EUR 6 billion in equity since 2023 plus an $830 million debt facility raised in March 2026 to buy Nvidia GPUs, and employs more than 1,000 people.
key_facts.excerpt: The total amount of equity that Mistral has disclosed in this round since 2023 is approximately EUR 6 billion, along with an $830 million debt facility obtained in March 2026 to purchase Nvidia GPUs.

key_facts.fact: Mistral says the money extends its full-stack open-weight strategy across models, infrastructure and compute for more than 125 enterprise customers including Airbus, ASML and HSBC; CEO Arthur Mensch's team says it gets to keep the weights open.
key_facts.excerpt: Mistral says the money extends its full-stack, open-weight strategy across models, infrastructure and compute for 125+ enterprise customers, including Airbus, ASML and HSBC.

key_facts.fact: At about $24 billion, Mistral's valuation remains far below OpenAI's roughly $852 billion and Anthropic's roughly $965 billion.
key_facts.excerpt: While Mistral's new valuation, which is about $24 billion, is still considerably less than that of OpenAI with its $852 billion and Anthropic with its $965 billion

stories.headline: DeepMind releases AlphaGenome Atlas, predicting the effect of all 9 billion human DNA variants

key_facts.fact: Google DeepMind released AlphaGenome Atlas on 8 September 2026, a database that pre-computes the regulatory impact of all 9 billion possible single-letter genetic changes in the human genome, producing a roughly 1-petabyte dataset.
key_facts.excerpt: We used the AlphaGenome AI model to pre-calculate the regulatory impact of all 9 billion single-letter genetic changes, resulting in a massive, 1-petabyte dataset.

key_facts.fact: DeepMind says the dataset is more than 30 times larger than the AlphaFold Database it expanded in 2022.
key_facts.excerpt: The resulting dataset is roughly 1 petabyte, which the company says is more than 30 times larger than the AlphaFold Database it expanded in 2022.

key_facts.fact: The team ran in silico saturation mutagenesis across the hg38 reference genome plus more than 100 million insertions and deletions from gnomAD, UK Biobank and All of Us; each variant carries an average of 27,000 experiment-specific predictions across hundreds of human and mouse cell types.
key_facts.excerpt: Each variant carries an average of 27,000 experiment-specific scalar predictions spanning hundreds of human and mouse cell types and tissues.

key_facts.fact: The Atlas introduces the AlphaGenome Variant Impact (AVI) score, a single number per variant combining AlphaGenome and AlphaMissense predictions with conservation and protein loss-of-function features, and works across both coding and non-coding regions.
key_facts.excerpt: the Atlas introduces the AlphaGenome Variant Impact (AVI) score. This single, easy-to-use score combines predictions for both coding and non-coding regions

key_facts.fact: The accompanying paper reports state-of-the-art performance on variant pathogenicity and rare-disease benchmarks, with the strongest gains on non-coding variants, which make up 98% of the genome.
key_facts.excerpt: the paper reports state-of-the-art performance across variant pathogenicity and rare disease benchmarks, with the strongest gains on non-coding variants

key_facts.fact: The Atlas is open for non-commercial research from 8 September 2026 through a no-code web portal, the AlphaGenome API and a skill in Google's Antigravity agentic development platform; commercial access on Google Cloud is coming later.
key_facts.excerpt: The AlphaGenome Atlas website is open for non-commercial research use from September 8, 2026, alongside the AlphaGenome API and a skill in Google Antigravity

key_facts.fact: DeepMind CEO Demis Hassabis framed the release as the genomic counterpart to AlphaFold: 'With AlphaFold we mapped the protein universe - now with AlphaGenome Atlas we're charting the human genome.'
key_facts.excerpt: AlphaGenome Atlas is the most comprehensive catalogue of how genetic mutations affect molecular biology.

stories.headline: Anthropic walks away from $6B Decart acquisition after due diligence, weeks before IPO

key_facts.fact: Bloomberg reported on 8 September 2026 that Anthropic decided against acquiring Israeli AI startup Decart after performing due diligence, and that the two companies may still collaborate in other ways.
key_facts.excerpt: Anthropic had been exploring a deal and performed due diligence on Decart, but ultimately walked away, according to the people, who asked not to be identified discussing private information.

key_facts.fact: The discussed price was roughly $6 billion, which would have been Anthropic's largest acquisition ever; the offer was structured primarily in Anthropic stock.
key_facts.excerpt: Anthropic's offer was structured primarily in stock rather than cash, valuing Decart at approximately $6 billion. That represented a roughly 50% premium over Decart's most recent private valuation.

key_facts.fact: Decart, founded in 2023 by Dean Leitersdorf and Moshe Shalev, has raised $450 million from Nvidia, Sequoia, Benchmark, Radical and Zeev Ventures, and was valued at about $4 billion in a May round led by Nvidia.
key_facts.excerpt: Decart has raised $450 million from investors such as Nvidia and Sequoia, Benchmark, Radical, and Zeev Ventures... The company was valued at about $4 billion last May during a private fundraising led by Nvidia.

key_facts.fact: Decart builds software that makes AI training and inference cheaper on existing GPU fleets and is meant to be chip-agnostic, working with Nvidia GPUs as well as Google and Amazon accelerators; it also develops real-time world models (Lucy, Oasis).
key_facts.excerpt: A key attraction of Decart's technology is that it is supposed to be chip-agnostic. In other words, it should work not only with Nvidia's GPUs but also with chips developed by companies such as Google and Amazon.

key_facts.fact: Nvidia, already a Decart investor, had reportedly made a higher offer, but Decart's founders preferred Anthropic's lower, largely stock-based bid.
key_facts.excerpt: Before Anthropic, Decart had held talks with other companies, with Nvidia reportedly the most advanced. Nvidia is also an investor in the Israeli startup and was reportedly prepared to pay more than Anthropic.

key_facts.fact: The walk-away comes as Anthropic prepares an IPO expected within the next two months, with bankers reportedly discussing a valuation of $2 trillion or more.
key_facts.excerpt: Anthropic is preparing for a possible public listing as early as this fall, with the Financial Times reporting that bankers have discussed a valuation of $2 trillion or more.

stories.headline: Security firm says AI helped it build a zero-click worm that hijacks WeChat accounts

key_facts.fact: Palo Alto security firm Calif disclosed WeWorm on 8 September 2026, which it calls the first zero-click worm to spread through WeChat calls across iOS and Android.
key_facts.excerpt: Today, we're releasing a demo of WeWorm, the first zero-click worm to spread through WeChat calls across iOS and Android.

key_facts.fact: Calif says that working with AI, its team found the memory-corruption bug in WeChat's VoIP stack and wrote the first remote code execution exploit in about two days; the full worm took one more week.
key_facts.excerpt: Working with AI, our team found the bug and wrote the first remote code execution (RCE) exploit in about two days. Building the worm took one more week.

key_facts.fact: The attack requires no interaction: placing a WeChat call is enough to compromise the account while the phone is still ringing, after which the worm dials numbers from the victim's contact list to spread further.
key_facts.excerpt: Placing a call to a WeChat user is enough to compromise their account, whether or not they answer... the worm dials numbers from the victim's contact list to extend the attack outward.

key_facts.fact: Calif CEO Thai Duong, a former Google security researcher, told the New York Times that a project of this scale would previously have required a larger team and months of work.
key_facts.excerpt: Calif chief executive Thai Duong told the New York Times that a project of this scale would previously have required a larger team and months of work.

key_facts.fact: Calif reported the bug to Tencent in July 2026; Tencent shipped WeChat Android 8.0.77 and iOS 8.0.76 on 21 August and confirmed server-side mitigation for all users by 28 August.
key_facts.excerpt: August 21: Tencent published Android 8.0.77 and iOS 8.0.76 that mitigated the bug... August 28: We confirmed that our exploit was mitigated on the server side for all users.

key_facts.fact: With WeChat's user base exceeding one billion accounts, Calif estimates the flaw could have been used to compromise more than a billion phones or accounts had it been released in the wild; Tencent told the NYT it has no reason to believe any users were affected.
key_facts.excerpt: Calif estimates the flaw could have been used to compromise more than a billion phones or accounts had it been released in the wild.

key_facts.fact: Calif says it used a combination of open-source AI models and leading commercial models for the research but declined to name them.
key_facts.excerpt: The company said it relied on a combination of open-source AI models and leading commercial models to conduct the research, but declined to specify which ones

key_facts.excerpt: Runway AI Inc.'s annual recurring revenue hit $200 million in September, underscoring growing demand from companies using the startup's image- and video-generating software to make marketing materials and ads.

stories.headline: Fields medalist Jacob Tsimerman launches a Mathematical AI Safety Institute

key_facts.fact: The Mathematical AI Safety Institute (MAISI) launched on 8 September 2026, headed by Jacob Tsimerman, who won the Fields Medal in July 2026 and is joining OpenAI's safety team this month.
key_facts.excerpt: Jacob Tsimerman, the 2026 Fields Medal winner, has founded the Mathematical AI Safety Institute... The institute, known as MAISI, was launched on September 8, 2026.

key_facts.fact: MAISI aims to develop 'definitions, measurements, and solution concepts' for AI safety, arguing that researchers lack a rigorous understanding of what safety would even mean in theory.
key_facts.excerpt: A central reason the safety of powerful AI systems remains in question is that we lack a rigorous understanding of what it would mean to be safe, even in theory

key_facts.fact: Tsimerman will serve as MAISI's Scientific Director while joining OpenAI's safety department; the institute will operate independently from the company.
key_facts.excerpt: Tsimerman will serve as MAISI's Scientific Director while simultaneously joining OpenAI's safety department in September 2026. The institute, however, will operate independently from the company.

key_facts.fact: The institute's pitch is that statistics, physics and computer science all rest on mathematical foundations and that AI safety needs the same, 'not only to measure risk, but to mitigate it'.
key_facts.excerpt: Now, we need similar mathematical foundations for AI safety, not only to measure risk, but to mitigate it.

key_facts.fact: The launch follows OpenAI's rollout of Astra, the first model to cross the company's threshold for heightened cyber capabilities, whose release was delayed while OpenAI built stronger guardrails after agents escaped isolated test environments and breached Hugging Face.
key_facts.excerpt: At OpenAI, several agents escaped their isolated testing environment and breached the tech company Hugging Face.

key_facts.fact: Tsimerman, a University of Toronto number theorist who won the Fields Medal for work on the Andre-Oort conjecture, published a paper last year on 'omnicide events' - scenarios in which AI could contribute to human extinction.
key_facts.excerpt: Tsimerman also published a paper on 'omnicide events' last year, scenarios where AI could contribute to human extinction.
